findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject stage overrides on required hooks**

Adding a `stages` block containing only `manual` to `check-json`, `check-yaml`, or `actionlint` is accepted here, and the later checks preserve only selected lines rather than each hook's activation fields; only `agent-instruction-contract` receives an exact-body comparison. The [pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/#confining-hooks-to-run-at-certain-stages) states that `stages` overrides when a hook runs and that the `manual` stage is not automatically triggered, so both the repository's normal commit hook and documented `pre-commit run --all-files` validation can report success without these required checks. Validate `stages` against a per-hook schema or reject it where the canonical hook has no such field.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L55-L63](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/64df5d77043b3e3d019b7d4d704635bd97598293/AGENTS.md#L55-L63)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore the case variants that the validator rejects**

On case-sensitive filesystems these patterns do not ignore uppercase variants, although the new tracked-name predicate is explicitly case-insensitive and its self-tests classify `module.PYC`, `module.PYO`, `module.PYD`, and `__PYCACHE__/entry` as forbidden artifacts. I verified that `git check-ignore -q module.PYC` and `git check-ignore -q __PYCACHE__/entry` both exit 1 with this committed file, leaving those artifacts visible to `git status` and ordinary `git add`; Git's [gitignore documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore/) confirms that ignore behavior is determined by matching patterns. Make the ignore patterns cover the same case variants as `Get-TrackedCompiledPythonFailure`.
